religious_christian.description: Buildings primarily designed for Christian worship: churches, cathedrals, basilicas, abbeys, chapels, monasteries. Defined by cross-topped towers, Gothic arches, Romanesque apses, or Byzantine domes with Christian iconography.
religious_christian.not: Mosques, temples, synagogues, or secular buildings that were formerly churches.
religious_christian.examples: Notre-Dame de Paris, Cologne Cathedral, Hagia Sophia (when classified as a cathedral), Westminster Abbey.

religious_islamic.description: Buildings primarily designed for Islamic worship or scholarship: mosques, madrasas, Islamic mausoleums, dargahs. Characterized by minarets, pointed arches, and domes with crescent finials.
religious_islamic.not: Hindu or Buddhist temples even if located in Muslim-majority countries.
religious_islamic.examples: Masjid al-Haram, Blue Mosque, Imam Mosque, Shah Jahan Mosque.

religious_other.description: Places of worship for all non-Christian, non-Islamic traditions: Hindu temples, Buddhist temples and pagodas, Shinto shrines, Sikh gurdwaras, Jewish synagogues, Jain temples, Zoroastrian fire temples, stupas.
religious_other.not: Secular buildings with vague spiritual associations.
religious_other.examples: Angkor Wat, Kinkaku-ji, Golden Temple Amritsar, Temple Mount, Borobudur.

palace_castle.description: Palatial residences, royal courts, and fortified complexes: palaces, royal manors, castles, fortresses, citadels, walled fortifications. Includes structures now used as museums if their dominant physical form is palatial or fortified.
palace_castle.not: Government administrative buildings without palatial or fortified architecture. Churches inside castle complexes — classify by the dominant complex.
palace_castle.examples: Versailles, Forbidden City, Edinburgh Castle, Alhambra, Topkapi Palace.

tower.description: Free-standing vertical structures whose primary identity is their height: observation towers, communication towers, medieval towers, lighthouse towers, campaniles, minarets classified as standalone structures.
tower.not: Towers that are part of a larger complex (a castle turret is part of the castle).
tower.examples: Eiffel Tower, Tokyo Skytree, Leaning Tower of Pisa, Blackpool Tower.

monument_statue.description: Commemorative structures intended to honor a person, event, or idea: statues, obelisks, memorial columns, war memorials, cenotaphs, victory columns.
monument_statue.not: Religious statues integral to a temple complex (classify as the temple). Buildings that happen to be memorials (e.g., a memorial museum → museum_gallery).
monument_statue.examples: Statue of Liberty, Christ the Redeemer, Washington Monument, Nelson's Column.

arch_gate.description: Triumphal arches, ceremonial city gates, historic entrance gates.
arch_gate.not: Gatehouses of larger complexes (the gate to a palace → palace_castle).
arch_gate.examples: Arc de Triomphe, Brandenburg Gate, India Gate, Marble Arch.

bridge.description: Bridges and viaducts of all structural types: suspension, arch, stone, cable-stayed, historic, modern.
bridge.examples: Golden Gate Bridge, Tower Bridge, Rialto Bridge, Pont du Gard.

museum_gallery.description: Buildings whose primary public identity is as a museum or art gallery, where the building itself is notable. Does NOT apply to landmark churches or palaces that contain museum collections — use their structural category.
museum_gallery.not: Landmark churches or palaces that contain museum collections.
museum_gallery.examples: Louvre (pyramid entrance and museum complex), British Museum, Guggenheim Bilbao, Smithsonian Castle.

theater_opera_stadium.description: Performing arts venues and sports stadiums: opera houses, concert halls, amphitheaters, sports arenas, coliseums. Grouped because both share an enclosed large-capacity public assembly function.
theater_opera_stadium.examples: Sydney Opera House, Colosseum, La Scala, Wembley Stadium, Bolshoi Theatre.

railway_station.description: Railway stations, train terminals, and transport hubs recognized as architectural landmarks.
railway_station.examples: Grand Central Terminal, St Pancras Station, Gare du Nord, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus.

ruins_archaeological.description: Sites whose primary public interest is their status as ancient ruins or an archaeological site: excavated cities, ancient remains, ruined temples no longer in active use. Note: if a ruin is still visually identifiable as a specific structural type and well-preserved (e.g., intact Roman temple), classify as that type instead.
ruins_archaeological.examples: Pompeii, Petra, Machu Picchu (if classified as ruins), Stonehenge, Acropolis of Athens.

garden_park_fountain.description: Botanical gardens, public parks, formal palace gardens, decorative fountains, plazas, and landscape monuments where the designed landscape IS the landmark.
garden_park_fountain.not: A park that contains other landmark structures — classify the structure instead.
garden_park_fountain.examples: Trevi Fountain, Gardens of Versailles (standalone entry), Central Park (as a landscape), Keukenhof, Villa d'Este gardens.

modern_landmark.description: Iconic contemporary buildings and structures built approximately after 1950 where the architectural innovation or iconic form is the defining quality, not a specific functional type. CONFLICT RESOLUTION: When a modern building fits both this category and another (e.g., Sydney Opera House), prefer the functional category. Use modern_landmark only when no functional category fits well.
modern_landmark.not: Modern towers (use tower). Modern stadiums (use theater_opera_stadium).
modern_landmark.examples: Burj Khalifa, Sagrada Família (ongoing construction), Guggenheim Bilbao (if iconic form dominates).

other_heritage.description: Any landmark that does not clearly fit categories 1–14. Use it for: historic districts and urban ensembles, harbors and canals, industrial heritage sites (mills, factories, aqueducts), historic universities and hospitals, natural named formations, lighthouses, historic town squares, military cemeteries, and any entity where forcing another label would be inaccurate.
other_heritage.examples: Canal Grande Venice (waterway), Mont-Saint-Michel (composite island/abbey), historic city walls, Suez Canal.

natural_landmark.description: Named, geographically fixed natural formations with no significant built structure: mountains, volcanoes, canyons, waterfalls, caves, rock formations, glaciers, islands as geographic landmarks.
natural_landmark.not: National parks (use other_heritage). A natural site that contains a significant built structure — classify by the built structure.
natural_landmark.examples: Mount Fuji, Grand Canyon, Victoria Falls, Ha Long Bay, Niagara Falls.
